projects.description:
IOM continues to strengthen central and municipal capacities on voluntary return and reintegration, supporting the implementation of Regulation 01/2018. Two workshops will be organized in 2026 to advance policy dialogue and strategic planning with MCR and other stakeholders. Four displaced families will be supported with housing, Harmonization Assistance Package (HAP) and Income Generating assistance (with a focus on female members of the family). 
To prepare for the upcoming EU‑funded RRK VI, IOM is reviewing over 480 applications in the MCR database and conducting socio‑economic and technical assessments with MCR and municipalities. At least 100 eligible displaced families will be identified for prioritized return and reintegration assistance.

projects.name: Promoting Rural Women`s Empowerment in Kosovo (FAO)
projects.description:
The project aims to remove structural barriers and address harmful gender norms, limited ownership of resources in agricultural and related sectors, introduce time and labour-saving technologies and provide innovative financing sources. It builds upon the findings and recommendations of the Kosovo Gender Profile on Agriculture and Rural Livelihoods. By implementing gender-responsive approaches and community mobilization, the intervention seeks to create a positive trajectory towards gender equality, economic empowerment, and sustainable rural development in Kosovo. Rural women will have better access to opportunities to increase their knowledge and skills and access resources for income-generation through sustainable agriculture. Secondly, the institutional environment and community engagement will be improved, enabling the implementation of gender-responsive actions.

The project focuses on three municipalities, highly affected by flooding, supporting their recovery and agricultural development, targeting disadvantaged groups.

Rural women, particularly those from disadvantaged communities and those facing risks of gender-based violence, along with local partners are the main target of this intervention. Their capacities in sustainable income generation in agricultural short-value chains with the potential for women's economic empowerment will be strengthened.

projects.name: Enhanced Pandemic Readiness and Emergency Planning for Action and Resilience Efforts
projects.description: The project will establish a cross-border electronic surveillance platform under a One Health framework for real-time, multi-sector, and multinational data sharing. It aims to strengthen laboratory networks by upgrading facilities, improving specimen transport, pursuing lab accreditation, and training personnel in biosafety, biosecurity, and advanced diagnostics. Additionally, it will develop a cross-sectoral workforce, including health, veterinary, agriculture, and community health personnel, to enhance early detection and coordinated outbreak response. The project design fosters collaboration across ministries and institutions, aligning policies across MAK through a regional coordination mechanism supported by the Institutes of Public Health. This mechanism will promote policy alignment to identify gaps in disease response, conduct gender and equity assessments, and implement a One Health RCCE strategy focused on AMR, zoonoses, and inclusive, community driven outbreak preparedness.

projects.name: Support to strengthening sustainable and multipurpose forest management to improve rural livelihoods and address climate change in Kosovo
projects.description:
The Programme Outcome is that Kosovar forests in target regions are managed more efficiently through a multi-purpose, participatory approach, strengthened in accordance with relevant rules on forests and supported with gender-responsive value-chains for poverty alleviation.
Programme is structured around three components, each further operationalized into specific outputs and activities. The first component is dedicated to improving timber legality, trade and law enforcement in forest sector. Outputs aim at preparing the necessary by-laws, improving public service capacities to support law enforcement with new skills and equipment, and generate public support to combat illegal activities in the forest sector. The second component aims at enhancing transparency and strengthening institutional capacity in good governance and implementation of forest policies, strategies and programmes. Key outputs should bring the Kosovo Forest Information System into a fully operational stage, help implement and re-formulate the PSP on Forestry Sector Development through gender mainstreaming, and support Kosovo in implementing its key forest sector programmes, such as the National Afforestation and Reforestation Programme and National Forest Health Programme.
The third component introduces and implements multi-purpose forest management, strengthens inclusive forest value chains for poverty alleviation of rural women and men, and aims to develop new skills and capacities in forest fire management.
projects.outcome: 3.3. Policies and capacities at central and local levels are strengthened to support sustainable natural resource management, climate change adaptation and mitigation, and enhanced resilience to natural disasters, particularly for vulnerable and at-risk communities.
